tagline: A First Class yacht for 16, refurbished in 2025, with two naturalist guides.
answer: Monserrat is Vianatura's 28-metre First Class motor yacht, built in 2005 and refurbished in 2025. She carries 16 guests in 10 cabins, including two single cabins and triple-capable cabins, with 9 crew and 2 naturalist guides. Four core routes of 3 or 4 nights combine into cruises of up to 14 nights, from US$2,795 per person in 2027. Children of all ages are allowed.

overview: Monserrat is a 28-metre motor yacht built in 2005 and refurbished in 2025, owned and run by Vianatura (Via Natura), a travel company with offices in Quito, Guayaquil, Cusco and Puerto Ayora. Vianatura's blog says she was built for 20 passengers and is now capped at 16, and that the September 2025 refit updated every cabin and social space.

Her ten cabins are on two decks. The Lower Deck has two single cabins and two double or twin cabins that take a third guest; the Upper Deck has six convertible doubles with large windows. All have private bathrooms and air conditioning. On board there is an observation lounge, two restaurants including the Latitude restaurant, a bar, a boarding lounge and a sundeck with a jacuzzi, two lounges and al fresco dining.

Four core routes, A and B of 4 nights and C and D of 3 nights, run back to back and combine into 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 or 14-night cruises. Two naturalist guides sail with 16 guests, which Vianatura puts at a 1 to 8 ratio.
why: Two naturalist guides for 16 guests on a First Class yacht, and single cabins with no solo supplement, per Vianatura, which is rare in the islands.
The four short routes stack into almost any length from 3 to 14 nights, and the whole yacht charters for 16 from US$44,795 in 2027. It pairs with Vianatura's Hermes for a two-tier offer.
